blocks.text:

The SAS has undergone some daring missions throughout its dramatic history.
Daring operations in London, Iraq and North Africa have inspired several dramatic films.
Here are five SAS operations that inspired Hollywood films.
## Operation Nimrod and _6 Days_
The 1980 Iranian Embassy Siege in London remains one of the SAS’s most famous operations.
Codenamed Operation Nimrod, the assault saw black-clad operators storm the embassy after a six-day siege to rescue hostages.

The events directly inspired the 2017 film _6 Days_, starring Jamie Bell and Mark Strong. The film recreated the tense negotiations and final assault, which was watched live by millions around the world.
## The Iranian Embassy Siege and _Who Dares Wins_
The success of Operation Nimrod in London also influenced the 1982 action film _Who Dares Wins_, released as _The Final Option_ in some countries.
Although fictional, the film drew heavily on public fascination with the SAS following the embassy siege.
It portrayed a special forces unit carrying out a daring counter-terrorist mission and helped introduce the regiment’s capabilities to international audiences.
## The Bravo Two Zero patrol and _Bravo Two Zero_
The Bravo Two Zero patrol took place in Iraq during the Gulf War in 1991.
The eight-man team was tasked with locating Scud missile launchers deep behind enemy lines. After being compromised, the patrol endured a gruelling fight for survival.
The story became a bestselling book by Andy McNab and was later adapted into the 1999 film _Bravo Two Zero_, starring Sean Bean.
## The Chris Ryan escape and _The One That Got Away_
The same Gulf War mission in Iraq inspired _The One That Got Away_.
During the Bravo Two Zero operation, SAS trooper Chris Ryan undertook a solo escape across the Iraqi desert after the patrol was discovered.
His journey became one of the longest successful escapes in British military history and was adapted into a television film.
## SAS operations in the Second World War and _The Devil’s Brigade_
Several wartime SAS raids in North Africa inspired elements of films including _The Devil’s Brigade_.
The daring attacks behind enemy lines, carried out under founder David Stirling, helped establish special operations tactics later portrayed in war films.
Jeep raids, sabotage missions and surprise attacks provided filmmakers with a rich source of inspiration for decades.

Not every migrant boat can be intercepted, a Cabinet minister has suggested, after two uncontrolled landings from the Channel in two days.
Education Secretary Lucy Powell said “(you) can’t stop everything all of the time”, the day after 21 people were detained when a boat evaded Border Force to reach the beach of Samphire Hoe in Dover.
It was the second undetected landing in two days, following a dinghy making it to shore at Folkestone on Monday morning.
The failure to intercept two migrant boats in two days before they reached the Kent coast was “not acceptable”, Shabana Mahmood has said.
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, who has ordered an urgent review by the Border Security Command, said the failure to intercept the two boats was “not acceptable”.
Ms Powell echoed that language on Thursday, while suggesting not all crossings could be prevented.
Asked on BBC Radio 4’s Today programme if the situation was embarrassing for the Government, she responded: “(You) can’t stop everything all of the time.
“Of course, it’s a concern. That’s why the Home Secretary has demanded and ordered this urgent review, because this is not what we want to see. This is not acceptable.

“But the overall picture is an improving picture. It is hard, difficult work that requires constant, constant effort by our border forces, our security services, police, our partnerships with France and other countries.

![Education Secretary Lucy Powell walking outside, carrying a folder](//image.assets.pressassociation.io/v2/image/production/0743a859362defd5b8fc2dcd873da4d6Y29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzkwMzIzNzM3/2.85861648.jpg?w=640)
Cabinet minister Lucy Powell said uncontrolled migrant boat arrivals are ‘a concern’ (Gareth Fuller/PA)
“This is a mammoth and huge task, which is now starting to reap some dividends. But of course, you know where there are still issues arising, we must absolutely tackle them.”
Pressed on Good Morning Britain whether she stood by her statement, Ms Powell said: “I think you’re just taking that completely out of context.
“We are clamping down on small boat crossings every single day… we are sucking the oxygen out of it, we are taking steps, and there are many, many steps.
“It’s not an easy thing to do to just turn on a switch, turn off a switch overnight. We have to constantly evolve.”

![Shabana Mahmood smiling while walking on Downing Street, carrying a red ministerial folder](//image.assets.pressassociation.io/v2/image/production/408acbbb7df705df7ec0534733146ce6Y29udGVudHNlYXJjaGFwaSwxNzkwMjY4NzE4/2.85861366.jpg?w=640)

Uncontrolled landings are so rare that last year’s incident was the only other one recorded since the Home Office began keeping data in 2023.
It will come as a blow to Border Security Command, which had suggested they were a thing of the past thanks to new surveillance technology and improved resources.
Shadow home secretary Chris Philp said: “Labour have admitted they will never stop the boats.
“Keir Starmer’s pledge to ‘smash the gangs’ was always a farce, and open-borders Burnham has learnt absolutely nothing from his predecessor.
“The only way to stop the crossings is to deport all illegal immigrants on arrival, and only the Conservatives have a plan to do that.”

**EXCLUSIVE:** The new boss of the UK’s influential Royal Television Society (RTS) thinks the charity should shout louder about the nation’s “powerhouse” TV industry to those who matter.
Sophie Jones said “there is a space for the RTS to ensure that the value of television as as whole is heard and understood by people who influence it.”

“That includes politicians, as well as people in the media who help shape the debate around the major decisions affecting the industry,” she said. “There is more we can do to champion television’s value as both a cultural and economic powerhouse in the UK.”
She stressed that the RTS “cannot – and will not – be a campaigning organization,” but there are still levers it can pull.

Jones took over from Theresa Wise three weeks ago and was [speaking exclusively to Deadline](https://deadline.com/2026/04/royal-television-society-unveils-ceo-sophie-jones-1236873227/) as she prepares to host her first RTS Convention, which takes place at London’s King’s Place on Tuesday and is this year chaired by Amazon. The convention takes place every year and switches venue between London and Cambridge.

The former Channel 4 corporate chief said the charity will “not have a view” on thorny issues like Israel-Palestine but “its role is to convene these conversations,” and if they sometimes prompt “controversial viewpoints, we have to deal with them as clearly as possible.” She was addressing the messy controversy the society became embroiled in last year after scrapping a special award for journalists in Gaza [before subsequently U-turning](https://deadline.com/2025/03/rts-special-gaza-award-program-awards-march-25-1236329393/) after facing pressure from all corners of the industry. “We will never take sides but we will continue to do the important work we do” while being clear about the correct “procedures and frameworks,” explained Jones.

The RTS Convention continues to nurture a repuation as one of the buzziest UK industry events and this year is no different, with talks from Jeremy Clarkson, Graham Norton and Steven Knight, along with top brass at the BBC and Channel 4, Matt Brittin and Priya Dogra, both of whom may feel they have to address the [hundreds of layoffs](https://deadline.com/2026/09/bbc-announce-tv-radio-closures-bbc-three-1237111317/) being enacted at their respective institutions.

It was the second undetected landing in two days, following a dinghy making it to shore at Folkestone on Monday morning.
The failure to intercept two migrant boats in two days before they reached the Kent coast was “not acceptable”, Shabana Mahmood has said.
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood, who has ordered an urgent review by the Border Security Command, said the failure to intercept the two boats was “not acceptable”.
Ms Powell echoed that language on Thursday, while suggesting not all crossings could be prevented.
Asked on BBC Radio 4’s Today programme if the situation was embarrassing for the Government, she responded: “(You) can’t stop everything all of the time.
“Of course, it’s a concern. That’s why the Home Secretary has demanded and ordered this urgent review, because this is not what we want to see. This is not acceptable.

“But the overall picture is an improving picture. It is hard, difficult work that requires constant, constant effort by our border forces, our security services, police, our partnerships with France and other countries.

Cabinet minister Lucy Powell said uncontrolled migrant boat arrivals are ‘a concern’ (Gareth Fuller/PA)
“This is a mammoth and huge task, which is now starting to reap some dividends. But of course, you know where there are still issues arising, we must absolutely tackle them.”
Pressed on Good Morning Britain whether she stood by her statement, Ms Powell said: “I think you’re just taking that completely out of context.
“We are clamping down on small boat crossings every single day… we are sucking the oxygen out of it, we are taking steps, and there are many, many steps.
“It’s not an easy thing to do to just turn on a switch, turn off a switch overnight. We have to constantly evolve.”

![Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has ordered an urgent review following the undetected boat arrivals (PA)](<data:image/svg+xml,%3Csvg xmlns='http://www.w3.org/2000/svg' viewBox='0 0 4000 2976'%3E%3C/svg%3E>)
Home Secretary Shabana Mahmood has ordered an urgent review following the undetected boat arrivals (PA)
The thousands of migrants crossing the Channel are usually brought to shore by Border Security Command or RNLI boats.
Before Monday, no small boat arrivals to the UK coast without an escort had been officially recorded since September 6, 2025.
Uncontrolled landings are so rare that last year’s incident was the only other one recorded since the Home Office began keeping data in 2023.
It will come as a blow to Border Security Command, which had suggested they were a thing of the past thanks to new surveillance technology and improved resources.
Shadow home secretary Chris Philp said: “Labour have admitted they will never stop the boats.
“Keir Starmer’s pledge to ‘smash the gangs’ was always a farce, and open-borders Burnham has learnt absolutely nothing from his predecessor.
“The only way to stop the crossings is to deport all illegal immigrants on arrival, and only the Conservatives have a plan to do that.”
